$comment: Research source register. Every factual claim in data/*.json must cite one or more ids from this file. reliability: primary (factory/AGCO publication), secondary-reference (published book or curated reference site), supplier (parts vendor listing), community (forum post), aggregator (spec site with unknown provenance). accessed=false means the source is known to exist but has not yet been read by this project.

sources.name: Wikipedia: Massey Ferguson 35
sources.reference: Main article; most claims cite Thorne (2014), see SRC-025
extracted: First FE35 (serial 1001) built 27 Aug 1956 at Banner Lane, Coventry; UK launch 1 Oct 1956
Colour: grey/gold at launch; standard MF red and grey from December 1957
Rebadged MF35 in 1957 after 73,655 units (UK)
Perkins diesel introduced in 1959 after MF bought Perkins
De Luxe models had a dual clutch that disengages the rear wheels while keeping PTO and hydraulic pump engaged
MF35X launched 8 Nov 1962; UK production ended 1964 (succeeded by MF135)
conflicts: Rebadge 'after 73,655 units' vs SRC-002 year table giving 1958 start at 79553

sources.name: Anglo Agriparts: Massey Ferguson 35, FE35, 35X Serial Numbers
sources.reference: Coventry serial-by-year table and model identification table
extracted: Engine listed for 1957-1959: Standard 23C diesel
Perkins 3.152 'from serial no. 165596'
Serial number location: dashboard (MF35); instrument panel (MF35X)
conflicts: Identification table says FE35 'up to serial No 74655' for 1956-57, inconsistent with its own year table

sources.name: Anglo Agriparts: Ferguson FE35 Serial Numbers
sources.reference: Prefix letter table; plate and engine-number locations; casting date codes
extracted: Same FE35 year-start serials as SRC-002 (final FE35 220613)

Prefix letters: chassis S=standard/wide front, C=high clearance, R=row crop twin front, T=row crop single front, J=industrial, V=vineyard, U=utility/turf; fuel G=gasoline, H=high-altitude gasoline, D=Standard diesel, K=TVO, L=lamp oil, P=Perkins diesel, B=LPG; clutch M=dual-stage, F=single-stage, W=Multi-Power
Page states some prefixes apply only to UK-built tractors and others only to early MF tractors
Serial plate at varying positions on the instrument console depending on model
Standard Motor engines have no plate; diesel engine data stamped into block just above the generator, right-hand side
UK casting date codes are day/month/year; FE35 codes on right side of differential/hydraulic housing forward of the round port
Diesels use the Standard 23C with Lucas electrical components

sources.name: TractorData: Ferguson FE-35
extracted: 6-speed unsynchronised gear transmission
Rear PTO 540 rpm: transmission-driven (special) or live (deluxe)
Differential shoe brakes; manual steering; weight 3093 lb / 1402 kg

sources.name: TractorData: Ferguson FE-35 engine
extracted: Standard 23C diesel: 4 cylinders, 137.89 cu in / 2.3 L, compression 20:1, firing order 1-3-4-2, liquid cooled, 12 V starter, 34 hp
conflicts: 34 hp vs 35.9 belt hp (SRC-006) vs 37 hp (SRC-011): rating basis not stated

sources.name: Agriline (South Africa): Standard 23C engine data
extracted: Bore 84.137 mm, stroke 101.6 mm, 2259 cc, compression 20:1, 35.9 belt hp, firing order 1-3-4-2
Main journal 69.901 mm; big-end journal 58.712 mm; gudgeon pin OD 28.579 mm; piston dia 84.010 mm
Valve clearance cold: inlet 0.305 mm, exhaust 0.203 mm; seat angle 45 deg
Starter Lucas M45G (11-tooth pinion); injection pump CAV DPA 3240011; injector break pressure 130 atm
Dynamo Lucas C45X (6 V) or Lucas C39P/2 (12 V)
Torques: head 110 Nm, main 40 Nm, con-rod 95 Nm, flywheel 135 Nm
conflicts: Main-bearing torque (40 Nm) lower than con-rod torque (95 Nm) is implausible and may be transposed; torque values are NOT to be displayed as confirmed until checked against the service manual (SRC-030/SRC-031)

sources.name: Wikipedia: Standard wet liner inline-four engine
extracted: 23C followed the 20C in 1956; bore 84.14 mm (3 5/16 in); 2,260 cc
MF stopped using Standard engines in favour of Perkins in 1959
After Leyland took over Standard-Triumph (1961) the engine became the Leyland OE.138
conflicts: Article family title is 'wet liner' but SRC-008 lists 23C as dry liner; 23C sentence is uncited

sources.name: Walt's Tractors: FE-35, TO-35 with 23C Standard Diesel
extracted: 3.3125 in bore, dry liner
Pistons offered with 4-ring or 5-ring sets
Rod and main bearings in std, .010, .020, .030, .040 undersize; separate thrust washers
Timing chain 62 pitches, chain tensioner, camshaft sprocket, crankshaft sprocket
Inner and outer valve springs; valve guides separate
Oil filter cartridge listed as replacing 826137M91, fits 20C and 23C
conflicts: Numeric cross-references (e.g. 191298, 391342) are of unknown origin and are NOT treated as OEM numbers

sources.name: Ferguson Club: Coldridge Collection articles
extracted: 23C combustion chamber developed by Freeman Sanders
Most 35s with the 23C did not have heater plugs in each cylinder; cold-climate option existed
23C described as a poor starter; MF evaluated Perkins P3 and F3 conversions c.1958
MF adopted Perkins A3.152 in production MF35 in 1959

sources.name: Southern Star: Massey Ferguson 35 had big boots to fill
extracted: Sold as 'standard' or 'deluxe'; deluxe added cushioned seat, dual-stage clutch and dash tractormeter
6 forward / 2 reverse gearbox split over high and low ratios; left lever gears 1-3 and reverse; right lever high/low and neutral 'start' position; gear pattern cast into housing
Dual clutch: half depressed disengages transmission but keeps PTO and hydraulics; fully depressed disengages both
Twin-lever control governing draft and implement height
Differential lock fitted (date not given)
conflicts: Differential lock introduction date not stated; may not apply to all 1958 tractors

sources.name: tractordata.co.uk: Massey Ferguson MF 35 4 Cylinder Diesel 1958
extracted: Diesel rated 37 hp (same as petrol); TVO 30 hp
Dual clutch, live PTO and hydraulics listed as Deluxe-only
conflicts: Claims hydraulics Deluxe-only; owner's tractor has hydraulics regardless, and other sources do not restrict hydraulics to Deluxe

sources.name: Agriline Products (UK): Ferguson FE35 4cyl hydraulic parts
extracted: Hydraulic pump OEM refs 184472M93, 184473M1, 184473M93 (10 spline)
Pump piston 23.1 mm, '2 required', from serial 65685; valve chamber assembly from serial 65685
Ram piston ring set 3 in from serial 65685; 2.5 in ring set up to serial 65684
Draft control spring, plunger, plunger seat, rocker, nut, locking knob listed as separate parts
Cross-shaft (rockshaft) bushes 60.2 x 50.8 x 35.8 mm, 4 per tractor; lift arms 37 splines
Relief valve 2300/2800 psi listed (application not stated)
conflicts: Pump piston count: '2 required' here vs pump description in community sources; needs parts-book confirmation

sources.name: Sparex S.40843 hydraulic pump repair kit (via masseytractorparts.com)
extracted: Kit: 2 x valve chamber assembly, 2 x piston, 2 x cam block (front/rear), 4 x piston rings, O-ring kit
Stated OEM equivalent 1810858M91; fitment list includes MF35 and TO35 without serial ranges

sources.name: TractorByNet: MF 35 Hydraulic Pump thread
extracted: Three pump versions used on MF35; 184473M92 with strainer and ringless pistons before serial 230456 (gas) / 231715 (diesel)
Replacement piston 190799M1, rings 892604M1; valve chamber 184471M1 common to all three
Front and rear camshaft blocks 180924M1 / 180925M1 fit inside the pistons and contact the camshaft
conflicts: Serial breaks may refer to US-built MF35 numbering; do not apply to Coventry serials without confirmation
